question: What is the total number of languages listed under the 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India, as on 30 June 2024? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 20
22
26
16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 22

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, under Articles 344(1) and 351, lists the official languages. As of 30 June 2024, there are 22 languages in this schedule. Originally, the Constitution included 14 languages, which were later increased through amendments. Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment (1992); and Maithili, Dogri, Santali, and Bodo were added by the 92nd Amendment (2003). These languages represent the diverse regional languages of India, and the government promotes their preservation and development.

question: Which of the following articles in the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice? (RRB ALP CBT 1 (16/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 84
Article 74
Article 70
Article 50
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 74

Explanation:
Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. This article forms the bedrock of the parliamentary system of government in India, where the real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers while the President acts as the constitutional head. The 42nd Amendment (1976) made it binding on the President to follow the advice of the Council of Ministers. However, the Supreme Court later clarified that the President can send the advice back for reconsideration. Article 74 thus ensures the principle of collective responsibility and democratic governance in India.

question: How many members are elected to the Public Accounts Committee from Rajya Sabha? (RRB ALP CBT 1 (16/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: 15
7
22
5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 7

Explanation:
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is one of the most important standing committees of Parliament, responsible for auditing the government's expenditures. It consists of a total of 22 members, out of which 15 members are elected from Lok Sabha and 7 members from Rajya Sabha. The members are elected by the method of proportional representation using the single transferable vote. The term of the committee is one year. It was first formed in 1921 under the Government of India Act 1919. After independence, it was given the status of a parliamentary committee in 1950. By convention, the chairman of the committee is appointed from the Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha.

question: Which of the following articles is INCORRECTY matched with the Constitutional Provisions related to Parliament ? (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 93 ----Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of People
Article 99 ---Composition of the Council of States/Rajya Sabha
Article 89---- Chairman and Deputy Chairman of Council of States
Article 105--- Powers and Privileges of the Houses of Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 99 ---Composition of the Council of States/Rajya Sabha

Explanation:
Article 99 relates to Oath or affirmation by members of Parliament, not the composition of the Council of States. Article 93 deals with the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People, Article 89 deals with the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and Article 105 deals with the Powers and Privileges of the Houses of Parliament. The composition of the Rajya Sabha is actually covered under Article 80, which provides for the composition of the Council of States (election of members from states and union territories). Article 99 specifically requires every member of Parliament to take an oath or affirmation before taking their seat. Therefore, matching Article 99 with the composition of Rajya Sabha is incorrect.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अनुच्छेद संसद से संबंधित संवैधानिक प्रावधानों के साथ सही सुमेलित नहीं है? (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)

अनुच्छेद 105 --- संसद के सदनों की शक्तियाँ और विशेषाधिकार

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 99 संसद के सदनों की संरचना के बजाय सदस्यों की शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 93 लोक सभा के अध्यक्ष और उपाध्यक्ष के बारे में है, अनुच्छेद 89 राज्यसभा के सभापति और उपसभापति के बारे में है, और अनुच्छेद 105 संसद के सदनों की शक्तियों और विशेषाधिकारों से संबंधित है। राज्यसभा की संरचना अनुच्छेद 80 में वर्णित है, जो राज्यसभा की संरचना (राज्यों और केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों से सदस्यों के चुनाव) से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 99 संसद के सदस्यों द्वारा शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान के बारे में है, न कि राज्यसभा की संरचना के बारे में। इस प्रकार, अनुच्छेद 99 का मिलान राज्यसभा की संरचना से करना गलत है।

question: Who among the following composed the National Song of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
Sri Aurobindo
Rabindranath Tagore
Sarojini Naidu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay

Explanation:
The National Song of India is 'Vande Mataram', composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. It was included in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882). It was adopted as the National Song on 24 January 1950 by the Indian Constitution. The song praises the motherland and served as an inspiration during the Indian independence movement. Rabindranath Tagore composed the National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana', while Sarojini Naidu is known as the 'Nightingale of India'. Sri Aurobindo was a philosopher and yogi. The music for 'Vande Mataram' was set by Rabindranath Tagore. This song is a symbol of Indian culture and nationalism.

question: The _______ takes the decision to declare any bill to be a money bill. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: President of India
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Governor of the Reserve bank of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker of the Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, the final decision to declare a bill as a Money Bill rests with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker's certificate on a Money Bill is considered final and binding and cannot be challenged in any court or by any other House. A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. If the Rajya Sabha does not return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed passed. The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration under Article 111.

☛ Where Money Bill is introduced → Only in Lok Sabha
☛ Role of Rajya Sabha → Can only make recommendations within 14 days
☛ Article 111 → President cannot withhold assent or return Money Bill
☛ Speaker's certificate → Final and cannot be questioned in any court

question: Which state under Article 371A has a special status? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Goa
Jammu and Kashmir
Nagaland
Puducherry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagaland

Explanation:
Article 371A is a special provision in the Indian Constitution that grants special status exclusively to the state of Nagaland. This article protects Naga religious or social practices, Naga customary law and procedure, and ownership of land and resources from being overridden by Parliamentary laws unless the state legislature passes a resolution. This provision was added in 1963 when Nagaland was formed, to safeguard the cultural and social identity of the Naga tribes. Other options, such as Goa (Article 371), Jammu and Kashmir (now repealed Article 370), and Puducherry (Union Territory) do not fall under this provision.

question: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country appointed by whom? (RRB ALP CBT 1 (18/02/2026) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following officially determines the constitutional validity of any legislation? (RRB ALP CBT 1 (18/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: The Parliament of India through a special resolution
The Supreme Court of India through judicial review
The President of India through constitutional discretion
The Union Cabinet through executive interpretation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Supreme Court of India through judicial review

Explanation:
In India, the official authority to determine the constitutional validity of any legislation rests with the Supreme Court, exercised through the power of judicial review. Judicial review allows the court to examine whether a law or executive order is consistent with the Constitution. If a law violates constitutional provisions, the Supreme Court can declare it unconstitutional. This power is enshrined in Article 13, 32, and 131-136 of the Constitution. The Supreme Court is also known as the Guardian of the Constitution.

question: Which among following fundamental duties is INCORRECT related towards the protection and promotion of scientific and cultural values? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: To safe guard the public property and to abjure violence
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To safe guard the public property and to abjure violence

Explanation:
Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists fundamental duties. Duty (i) 'To safeguard public property and to abjure violence' relates to social and national security, not to the protection and promotion of scientific and cultural values. Duties related to scientific and cultural values are duty (j) 'To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture', duty (h) 'To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform', and duty (k) 'To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity'. Among these, duty (k) is directly linked to scientific and cultural progress by promoting excellence. Hence, duty (i) is incorrectly related.

question:
Which among the following changes were made in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act ?
(RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Nationalization of Land Ceiling Laws.
Introduction of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.
Inserted Right to Privacy in the Article 21 of Indian Constitution.
Increased Lok Sabha seats from 525 to 545.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Introduction of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A

Explanation:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 1976. It introduced Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution under Article 51A, providing a list of 10 duties for citizens, such as to defend the nation and protect public property. This amendment also added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It attempted to reduce the power of judicial review, but the Supreme Court later upheld it. Nationalization of land ceiling laws or the Right to Privacy were not part of this amendment. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini Constitution' due to its extensive changes.

question: Which among the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides Municipalities with financial powers? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)

solution:

Article 40 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the state to organize village panchayats. This act added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) to the Constitution, dealing with panchayats. It came into force on April 24, 1993, celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day. While Article 40 existed in the original Constitution, the 73rd Amendment strengthened it by providing a uniform structure for local self-government.

question: The impeachment of President due to violation of the the Constitution is preferred by _____________. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Only Lok Sabha
Only Rajya Sabha
Either House of the Parliament
Only Speaker of Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Either House of the Parliament

Explanation:
According to Article 61 of the Indian Constitution, the impeachment of the President for violation of the Constitution can be initiated by either House of the Parliament. The process begins when at least one-fourth of the members of that House sign a notice of the charge. The House then investigates the charge through a committee. If the committee finds the charge valid, the resolution is sent to the other House. The other House also investigates, and if passed by a two-thirds majority, the President is removed from office. This procedure can be initiated at any time during the President's term.

question: Which among the following information is NOT a ground for exemption from disclosure of information under RTI Act, 2005? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Breach of privilege of Parliament
Cabinet papers including records of deliberation
Sovereignty and integrity of India
Public Interest
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public Interest

Explanation:
Section 8(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 lists the grounds for exemption from disclosure of information. These include breach of privilege of Parliament (Section 8(1)(c)), Cabinet papers including records of deliberation (Section 8(1)(i)), and sovereignty and integrity of India (Section 8(1)(a)). Public Interest is not a ground for exemption; rather, it is a principle that encourages disclosure. Under Section 8(2), even exempted information can be disclosed if public interest outweighs the harm. Thus, public interest is not an exemption ground but an exception.

question: As per Article ___________ of the Indian Constitution, from the date of commencement of the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union territory of Delhi shall be called the National Capital Territory of Delhi. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 239AC
239AD
239AB
239AA
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 239AA

Explanation:
According to Article 239AA of the Indian Constitution, from the date of commencement of the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union territory of Delhi shall be called the National Capital Territory of Delhi. This provision grants Delhi a special status, including the formation of a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers. Article 239AA defines the governance framework for Delhi, covering the appointment of the Chief Minister and ministers, powers of the Legislative Assembly, and relations with the central government. This amendment gives Delhi a semi-state status, though subjects like police, land, and public order remain under central control. Articles 239AB and 239AC pertain to other administrative provisions, while 239AA is specifically for the National Capital Territory.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद _________ के अनुसार, संविधान (69वाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1991 के लागू होने की तिथि से दिल्ली केंद्र शासित प्रदेश को राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली कहा जाएगा। (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options_hi: 239AC

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 239AA

Explanation:

question: According to ____ of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament may by law, constitute a High Court for a Union territory. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 239
Article 238
Article 240
Article 241
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 241

Explanation:
Article 241 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to constitute a High Court for a Union territory by law. It also allows Parliament to extend the jurisdiction of an existing High Court to a Union territory or to exclude it. This article falls under Part VI of the Constitution. Article 239 deals with the administration of Union territories, Article 238 was repealed (it dealt with states), and Article 240 confers power to make regulations for certain Union territories. Thus, only Article 241 specifically addresses the creation of High Courts for Union territories.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किसके अनुसार, संसद कानून बनाकर, किसी केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए हाई कोर्ट बना सकती है। (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 239
अनुच्छेद 238
अनुच्छेद 240
अनुच्छेद 241
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 241

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 241 संसद को यह शक्ति देता है कि वह कानून बनाकर किसी केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए एक उच्च न्यायालय स्थापित कर सकती है। यह अनुच्छेद यह भी प्रावधान करता है कि संसद ऐसे उच्च न्यायालय के अधिकार क्षेत्र और शक्तियों को निर्धारित कर सकती है। इसके अलावा, संसद किसी मौजूदा उच्च न्यायालय के अधिकार क्षेत्र को केंद्र शासित प्रदेश तक विस्तारित कर सकती है। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग VI में आता है। अनुच्छेद 239 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है, अनुच्छेद 238 निरस्त कर दिया गया है, और अनुच्छेद 240 कुछ केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के लिए नियम बनाने की शक्ति देता है।
